title: Minify tier thickness to 6 nm for 1000-tier atomic stacks
idea: Grow alternating MOCVD 2D-semiconductor channel sheets (MoS2 or WSe2, about 1 nm) and hBN/oxide spacers (about 5 nm) so each tier is 6 nm and 1000 tiers fit in a 6 um stack. Gain-cell storage nodes are gated by shared vertical gate holes etched once per 100-tier deck, as in 3D NAND.
why: 3D break-even (26+ tiers): goes 40x past it at a stack height that an etcher can already reach; the wide bandgap of 2D channels also cuts leakage, so refresh could fall by more than 100x.
note: 1000 tiers at 6 nm pitch would be far past 10x density; doubt: sequential 2D growth/transfer yield.

title: Vertical CCD strings: 3D NAND geometry clocked as charge-coupled DRAM
idea: Revive 1970s CCD serial memory inside a 3D-NAND-like stack: a vertical gate-all-around oxide-semiconductor or poly channel with 128 wordline tiers is clocked in three phases to shift charge packets up and down, with one sense/regenerate amplifier at the string foot. There is no per-cell contact, capacitor or access transistor, and bidirectional shifting halves average latency.
why: Facts 1, 2 and 7: cell area approaches 3D NAND bit density (~10x DRAM per mm2) and one sense amp serves 128 bits; ~60-130 ns access fits the DRAM-class window for streaming data.
note: ~10x density via contactless vertical CCD; doubts: transfer loss over 128 poly/IGZO stages, serial not random access.

title: Plated-pillar memory: circumferential magnetization lining 3D NAND-style holes
idea: Revive Univac/Bell plated-wire memory vertically: etch high-AR holes through a stack of word-strap tiers, ALD a soft magnetic shell, spacer and reference layer down each hole, and store bits as circumferentially magnetized ring segments under each strap, sensed non-destructively by the magnetoresistance of an axial read current. Closed-flux rings have no stray field, so hole pitch can be tight.
why: Facts 2 and 8: a deposition-built 3D cell with non-destructive read, no capacitor and near-unlimited endurance; 3D NAND-like density at ~20-50 ns reads.
note: Deposition-built 3D cell with NDRO and unlimited endurance at NAND density; ALD magnetic quality and tiny MR signal are the doubts.

title: Matrix Semiconductor's write-once 3D ROM as a weights tier
idea: Matrix Semiconductor's 8-deck antifuse crosspoint (2001) failed because nobody wanted write-once storage. LLM inference does: burn model weights into a stack of antifuse decks over the accelerator's periphery, read in tens of ns. The weights no longer occupy DRAM, which then holds only KV cache and activations.
why: Does DRAM's job with less DRAM: weights are ~50-80% of inference memory, written once at ~10x DRAM's bits per mm2, with no refresh.
note: Hardwired weights offload DRAM; model churn limits value.

title: Photomultiplier read: avalanche gain junction under each pillar
idea: Like a photomultiplier or SPAD turning one photon into a pulse, place a quenched avalanche junction at the foot of each vertical bitline biased just below breakdown; a 0.1 fF cell's few hundred electrons trigger ~100x multiplication, then a passive quench resets it, so cells and lines stay tiny.
why: Capacitor wall and access energy (facts 1, 8): Cs drops ~50x and the local line stays a few fF; claims >10x lower energy per read if avalanche statistics and dark counts are tamed.
note: Avalanche gain lets Cs shrink ~50x; dark counts, gain noise and high bias fight the voltage floor.

title: Display fabs build IGZO memory tiers on Gen-8.5 glass panels
idea: [Box: 2T0C gain charge | IGZO TFT | current sense | many-tier panel-level stack | 2.2 x 2.5 m glass | i-line/ArF dry steppers in existing LCD/OLED fabs] Use idle display-fab capacity to build IGZO gain-cell arrays at ~0.5 um F on huge glass panels, stack 8-16 tiers, and dice them into CXL capacity-tier memory modules.
why: Capital intensity and supply: at 8F2, F=0.5 um gives ~60 GB/m2 per tier, ~340 GB per panel tier; glass costs ~100x less per m2 than processed Si, with no EUV.
note: ~$5/GB per tier on glass: above DDR5 cost but below contract price, with no EUV.

title: Weimer's 1962 TFT reborn: panel-fab memory on Gen-8 glass
idea: Revive RCA's thin-film transistor for memory: build 4-tier oxide-TFT DRAM-like arrays on Gen-8.5 glass in idle LCD and plasma panel fabs at ~1 um features, accept 1% defective cells across huge panels with block codes, and sell them as cheap capacity modules.
why: Capital intensity and U.S./allied manufacturability: panel fabs cost ~100x less per m2 than DRAM wafers; at 4 tiers cost could approach ~$10/GB with no EUV or quartz crucibles.

title: Gen-8.5 display glass replaces 300 mm wafers for capacity memory
idea: Substitute DRAM fabs with idle LCD/OLED backplane lines: use their IGZO TFT process on 2.2x2.5 m glass to build 4-8 stacked layers of relaxed-pitch (~0.8 um) oxide-semiconductor gain-cell arrays, dice into large memory tiles with a bonded small CMOS controller, and sell as CXL far-memory modules.
why: Capital intensity and EUV (fact 4): depreciated display capex, zero EUV, new supply outside the DRAM-fab bottleneck; ~30-50 GB per layer per panel, roughly $8-15/GB at 4-8 layers, competitive at today's 4x prices for a slower ~100-300 ns tier.
note: Depreciated Gen-8.5 IGZO lines add EUV-free capacity; doubt: 0.8 um pitch density and slow tier may not hold $/GB long term.

title: Turbine-blade eutectic solidification grows built-in vertical nanorod plates
idea: Borrowed from directionally solidified eutectic alloys used in turbine blades: solidify a Si-TaSi2 eutectic ingot so billions of aligned metallic TaSi2 nanorods run through monocrystalline Si, then slice wafers in which each rod is a ready-made vertical capacitor plate or buried bitline, with cells formed around them by one mask.
why: Self-organized vertical conductors replace high-AR etch and fill (facts 1,4); a ~100x path if fast growth brings rod pitch near ~100 nm; trade-off: irregular lattice needs per-die mapping.
note: Self-organized eutectic rods as pre-built vertical plates is unseen; rod pitch is microns at practical growth rates.

title: Oxygen: porous-silicon oxidation carves many SOI tiers from one epi stack
idea: Grow an epi stack alternating p+ (~1e19) and lightly doped Si, open slits, anodize in HF so only the p+ layers become mesoporous, then oxidize them at ~850 C into buried oxide (FIPOS); the lightly doped layers remain single-crystal device tiers.
why: Crystalline multi-tier SOI with no germanium (no SiGe mismatch limit on tier count) and no bonding cycles; attacks the lateral-transistor blocker (fact 2) at epi-reactor cost.
note: Porous-Si oxidation (FIPOS) carves many crystalline tiers without SiGe strain limits; boron diffusion and expansion stress are risks.

title: All-IGZO monolithic memory: n-only periphery in the same tiers
idea: TRIZ #33 Homogeneity: build sense amps, decoders and drivers from the same IGZO transistors as the 2T0C array, using bootstrapped n-only (pseudo-CMOS) circuits, so each BEOL tier is a complete memory with no CMOS underneath. The whole stack can sit on any logic die's metal stack.
why: Fact 5 and 7: memory micrometres above compute (~0.1-0.3 pJ/bit vs 3-4 pJ/bit HBM) and periphery needs no separate FEOL; any logic fab's BEOL becomes DRAM capacity.
note: Any logic BEOL becomes DRAM capacity; doubt: n-only IGZO sense amps are slow, variable and low-density.

title: Interposer-as-memory: oxide DRAM tiers in the passive interposer
idea: Under 400 C, build four oxide-channel 1T1C DRAM tiers in the BEOL of the large passive silicon interposer that already sits under the GPU and HBM, patterned with ArF at 40 nm. The interposer becomes about 100 GB of near memory directly under the compute die.
why: Facts 5 and 6: about 150 Mb per mm2 per tier on about 2500 mm2 of otherwise idle silicon, sub-pJ/bit access, no TSVs and no extra wafer.
note: Idle interposer BEOL becomes ~100 GB near memory at sub-pJ/bit; doubt: oxide 1T1C density at 40 nm and interposer cost.
